skills.name: esp32agent
skills.desc: See and drive a real iPhone through an ESP32 Agent board (the phone's mouse/keyboard over USB or Bluetooth + AirPlay screen mirroring, reached over Bluetooth). Use when asked to look at, tap, type on, or operate the iPhone, or to test an iOS app on the device.
skills.body:
---
name: esp32agent
description: See and drive a real iPhone through an ESP32 Agent board (the phone's mouse/keyboard over USB or Bluetooth + AirPlay screen mirroring, reached over Bluetooth). Use when asked to look at, tap, type on, or operate the iPhone, or to test an iOS app on the device.
---

# esp32agent

`esp32agent` talks to an ESP32 Agent board next to the iPhone. The board is the phone's mouse and keyboard and
receives its AirPlay screen mirroring; this computer reaches it over Bluetooth. Every command prints
JSON: `{"status":"ok","data":...}` or `{"status":"error","error":"..."}`. The MCP server (`esp32agent mcp`)
offers the same as tools: screenshot, tap, longpress, swipe, type_text, press_key, press_button, device_info,
plus history, intent_list, intent_show, intent_save, memory_recall and memory_add.

The board runs in one of two modes, set in the iOS app (Settings > Board > Input); the CLI cannot switch it:
- USB mode: plugged into the iPhone's USB-C port, it is the phone's USB mouse and keyboard.
- Bluetooth mode: it is the phone's Bluetooth mouse and keyboard, with no USB data to the phone; any USB power
  (charger, power bank) will do. Lightning iPhones (XS to 14) need this mode. `esp32agent device info` then has
  `hid`: `ok` while the phone's Bluetooth link to the board is up, else `off`.

## Setup (once)
- The board takes new pairings only in the first 3 minutes after it powers up: run `esp32agent pair` then.
  In Bluetooth mode the iPhone pairs the board in that same window (Settings > Accessibility > Touch >
  AssistiveTouch > Devices > Bluetooth Devices); the CLI pairs on its own, next to the phone. Missed it: unplug
  and replug the board's power (forgetting the device on the iPhone does not reopen it).
- Screen Mirroring on the iPhone: Control Center > Screen Mirroring > ESP32 Agent.
- `esp32agent calibrate` (also runs by itself on the first tap). It needs the mouse pointer visible on screen.

## The loop
1. `esp32agent screenshot` (writes a PNG in the current directory and prints its `filePath`; read the image).
   It waits until the screen has settled after your last action, so it never shows the screen from before it.
2. Decide one action from what you see.
3. Act, with coordinates in pixels of that screenshot (full size: don't pass `--scale`/`--max-size` if you
   take coordinates from it):
   - `esp32agent io tap X,Y` (add `--aim` after a missed tap: finds the pointer and corrects first; `--count 2` double-taps, e.g. to zoom a map or select a word)
   - `esp32agent io longpress X,Y --duration 1500`
   - `esp32agent io swipe X1,Y1,X2,Y2` (scroll a list: swipe up from the lower to the upper middle)
   - `esp32agent io text 'hello'`, `esp32agent io keys enter`, `esp32agent io keys cmd+a`
   - `esp32agent io button HOME` (Home Screen)
4. Screenshot again and check the result before the next step. Never chain several taps blind.

When the task depends on what the phone plays (a video, a call, a voice message, a spoken code),
`esp32agent listen` gives its words from the last 30 s, or says why the phone can't be heard (listening off,
the app not sharing, no Wi-Fi). The words can be partial or misheard; check the screen when it matters.

## Typing
- The board types printable ASCII only, one key per character.
- Chinese is typed as pinyin: `io text '拿铁'` types `natie` (the reply says `typed_as`). With the iPhone's Chinese (pinyin)
  keyboard active, commit the first candidate with `io keys space`, or screenshot and tap the right candidate.
  Many search boxes accept the plain pinyin as well.
- The board is a hardware keyboard, so iOS may hide the on-screen keyboard; the text field still takes the keys.
- Tap the text field first so it has focus; `io keys cmd+a` then `io keys backspace` clears it.
- Bluetooth mode: whether iOS takes modifier combos (`cmd+a`, `ctrl+space`, ...) from the board is being verified.
  Screenshot after one; if nothing changed, select the text with a long press (Select All) or a double tap on a
  word, then `io keys backspace`.

## Save what worked
After a task succeeded, save it so the next run is faster:
1. `esp32agent history show latest` (MCP: `history` with action show): the run's steps in 0-1000 screen units,
   numbered, each with the screenshot it was done on. Every action and screenshot is recorded by itself; a new run
   starts after 10 minutes idle, or with `esp32agent history new` before a new task.
2. Pick the steps that did the job (skip detours, misses and retries).
3. `esp32agent intent save --name 'Alarm 7:00' --prompt 'Set an alarm for 7:00 AM every day' --hint 'Type the time
   instead of scrolling the wheel' --from-run RUN --steps 2,3,5` (MCP: `intent_save` with name, prompt, hints,
   from_run, steps). One short, clear instruction as the prompt and at most 6 concrete hints. Only replayable moves
   can be steps: tap, swipe, type, key, home. The same name replaces the old intent.

## Run a saved intent
1. `esp32agent intent list`, then `esp32agent intent show NAME` (MCP: `intent_list`, `intent_show`): the prompt,
   hints and recorded steps, each with its reference screen (a JPEG path).
2. Follow the steps as references, not blindly: coordinates are 0-1000 units of the screen, so convert them to
   pixels of your screenshot (x * width / 1000, y * height / 1000).
3. Take a screenshot after each step and check it looks like the next step's reference screen.
4. On a mismatch (another screen, a popup, a changed layout) drop the recorded steps and go on with the normal loop,
   using the prompt and hints.

## Memory
- Before a task, `esp32agent memory search 'TASK'` (MCP: `memory_recall`): the user's preferences and how their apps
  work, the same entries the iOS app uses.
- When the user says to remember something, `esp32agent memory add 'TEXT' --kind preference` (MCP: `memory_add`).
  Only the user's own words; never passwords, codes or numbers off the screen.

## Errors to act on
- `busy: the app is using the phone`: the iOS app is driving right now. Wait and retry later; don't fight it.
- `screen mirroring is off`: ask the user to start Screen Mirroring to ESP32 Agent.
- `video frozen`: ask the user to stop and restart Screen Mirroring.
- `not paired` or `pairing window closed`: ask the user to replug the board (its power, in Bluetooth mode) and
  run `esp32agent pair` within 3 minutes.
- `phone usb asleep` (USB mode): the phone is locked; ask the user to unlock it.
- `Bluetooth HID not paired` or `typed N of M: asleep` (Bluetooth mode): the phone's Bluetooth link to the board
  is down. Ask the user to check that Bluetooth is on and the board shows Connected on the iPhone; if the phone
  never paired it, replug the board's power and pair it within 3 minutes.
- `not supported on ESP32 Agent`: there is no app list, UI tree, file access or webview; work from screenshots.

## Limits
- Video comes over Bluetooth: a screenshot can be up to a second behind, animations look choppy.
- Only HOME as a button (in Bluetooth mode iOS has no Home key, so it goes Home with Cmd+H or the swipe up from
  the home bar, which needs Screen Mirroring on); no volume, power, or app install/launch (open apps from the Home Screen or Spotlight:
  `io button HOME`, swipe down in the middle, `io text 'Settings'`, `io keys enter`).

skills.name: manina-run-tasks
skills.desc: Guides Siri through multi-step work with ESP32 Agent (Manina AI), which operates a real iPhone by looking at the screen and tapping, swiping and typing. Use when a request needs a phone task done or a recorded run replayed, and more than one step or tool may be involved.
skills.body:
---
name: manina-run-tasks
description: Guides Siri through multi-step work with ESP32 Agent (Manina AI), which operates a real iPhone by looking at the screen and tapping, swiping and typing. Use when a request needs a phone task done or a recorded run replayed, and more than one step or tool may be involved.
---

# Working with ESP32 Agent (Manina AI)

ESP32 Agent drives a physical iPhone through a board plugged into it. It sees the phone's screen and
moves the pointer, so it can do what a person would do by hand. Every task is one run, and every run
is recorded so it can be replayed.

Use the tools by what they do:

- **run a task on this iPhone** — starts a run from one sentence.
- **check the run** — whether the board, Screen Mirroring, the pointer and the model are ready,
  and what the current or last run is doing.
- **stop the run** — stops the run in progress.
- **replay a run** — opens a recorded run so the person can go through its steps.

## Turning a request into one task sentence

A run takes a single sentence describing the goal and the app to use in it. Write that sentence
from what the person said, in their language, then start the run.

Keep it to the goal, not to the steps. The run works out its own steps by looking at the screen,
so naming menus or buttons is wasted and can be wrong. The phone in the person's hand may differ
from what either of you expects.

Include the app when the request implies one. "Find cafés near me" is weaker than "Find cafés near
me in Google Maps", because the run has to start somewhere.

Ask one short clarifying question only when the goal is genuinely ambiguous — which app, or which
of two very different outcomes. Do not interview the person for details the run can see on screen.

## Before a run starts

Starting a run needs the board connected, Screen Mirroring on, the pointer calibrated and a model
chosen. The person sets these up in the app; no tool can do it.

When a run cannot start, it says what is missing. Relay that in one sentence and offer to open the
app, rather than retrying — the missing piece is on the phone, not in the request.

A run needs the person's agreement before screenshots and the task go to the model they configured.
If the run reports that, tell them to open ESP32 Agent and allow it, then ask again. Do not work
around it.

## While a run is going

A run puts the phone to work. The app goes to the Home Screen and the person watches progress in a
Live Activity, so the app is not in the foreground while the run works.

Do not start a second run while one is going: check the run, and offer to stop the current run
if the person wants the new one instead.

If the run says it needs help, it has stopped at a screen it cannot handle. Tell the person what it
is stuck on and let them decide: continue after they fix it, or stop. Never claim a run is still
going once it has asked for help.

## Replaying and reporting

Every run is recorded step by step with the screen it saw. To walk someone through what happened,
replay the run — it opens the same review screen a tap on the run in the list opens. Refer to runs by
the task sentence, and prefer the most recent one when the person says "the last one".

When reporting, say what the run did in plain words and whether it finished. Do not read out raw
steps or screen coordinates, and do not present a run that stopped early as done.

## Boundaries

The phone holds the person's accounts, messages and money. Before anything that spends money, sends
a message or email, posts, calls someone, deletes data, or changes a password or security setting,
ask the person to confirm, and pass the task along only after they agree.

If a task needs a password, passcode, Face ID or a one-time code, stop and hand it to the person.
Do not ask them to say such a value out loud to you.

Help: support@manina.ai

skills.desc: See and drive a real iPhone through an ESP32 Agent (Manina AI) board with the esp32agent CLI or MCP server. Use when asked to look at, tap, swipe, type on, or operate an iPhone, or to test an iOS app on a real device.
skills.body:
---
name: manina
description: See and drive a real iPhone through an ESP32 Agent (Manina AI) board with the esp32agent CLI or MCP server. Use when asked to look at, tap, swipe, type on, or operate an iPhone, or to test an iOS app on a real device.
license: MIT-0
metadata:
  openclaw:
    requires:
      bins: [npx, ffmpeg]
    envOptional: [ESP32AGENT_DEVICE]
    homepage: https://manina.ai
---

# Manina AI: drive a real iPhone with esp32agent

An ESP32 Agent board (Manina AI) acts as the iPhone's mouse and keyboard: plugged into a USB-C iPhone (USB mode),
or as its Bluetooth mouse and keyboard on any USB power (Bluetooth mode; Lightning iPhones XS to 14 need it). The
mode is set in the iOS app (Settings > Board > Input); the CLI cannot switch it. It also receives the iPhone's AirPlay screen mirroring. Your computer reaches
the board over Bluetooth with the `esp32agent` command line tool, which is also an MCP server. No jailbreak is
needed.

iPhone only for now. iPad support is coming soon.

## Prerequisites

- A Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32S3 board (8 MB flash, 8 MB PSRAM), or a similar ESP32-S3 board with native USB.
- Board firmware v0.2.2 or later. Install it in Chrome or Edge at https://manina.ai/install
  (one USB data cable, nothing else to install). Bluetooth mode needs v0.2.7 or later with both inputs.
- On the iPhone:
  - AssistiveTouch on (Settings > Accessibility > Touch > AssistiveTouch), so the mouse pointer shows and taps.
  - Screen Mirroring to the board: join the board's Wi-Fi, then Control Center > Screen Mirroring > ESP32 Agent.
  - The phone unlocked while the agent works.
- On the computer: Bluetooth, Node.js 18 or later (for `npx`), and `ffmpeg` (needed for screenshots).

## Install

Nothing to install up front; `npx` fetches the CLI:

```sh
npx -y esp32agent version
```

Or install it globally with `npm install -g esp32agent` and call `esp32agent` directly. The examples below use
`npx -y esp32agent`; with a global install, drop the `npx -y`.

MCP server (stdio), if your agent does not already have it from this plugin:

```sh
claude mcp add esp32agent -- npx -y esp32agent mcp
```

Other MCP clients:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "esp32agent": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "esp32agent", "mcp"] } } }
```

## Pair (once per computer)

1. Power the board (USB mode: plug it into the iPhone). Within 3 minutes of it powering up run
   `npx -y esp32agent pair`. In Bluetooth mode, pair the board on the iPhone in the same window (Settings >
   Accessibility > Touch > AssistiveTouch > Devices > Bluetooth Devices); missed it, replug the board's power.
2. Start Screen Mirroring on the iPhone to ESP32 Agent.
3. `npx -y esp32agent screenshot` should now save a PNG of the phone's screen.
4. `npx -y esp32agent calibrate` measures the pointer. It also runs by itself before the earliest tap. It needs
   the pointer visible on screen.

## MCP tools

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `screenshot` | The screen now, after the last action settled. Other tools take pixel coordinates of this image |
| `tap` | Tap at `x`, `y`; `count: 2` double-taps |
| `longpress` | Press and hold at `x`, `y` (`duration_ms`, default 1000) |
| `swipe` | Swipe from `x1`, `y1` to `x2`, `y2` |
| `type_text` | Type into the focused field (ASCII; Chinese is typed as pinyin) |
| `press_key` | `enter`, `esc`, `tab`, `backspace`, `space`, arrows, `cmd+a`, `shift+tab` ... |
| `press_button` | `HOME` only (go to the Home Screen) |
| `device_info` | Board status: mirroring (`ap`), video frozen (`fz`), app busy (`busy`), `usb`, `ble`; in Bluetooth mode `hid` (`ok`/`off`) |
| `history` | `action: list` (recent runs) or `show` (one run's steps with their screenshots) |
| `intent_list`, `intent_show`, `intent_save` | Saved tasks: list, show one, save what worked |

Every tool takes an optional `device` (board id) when more than one board is nearby.

## CLI commands

Every command prints JSON: `{"status":"ok","data":...}` or `{"status":"error","error":"..."}` (exit code 1).

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `devices` | Boards nearby (`id`, `paired`, `connected`) |
| `pair`, `unpair` | Pair this computer with the board; forget it here |
| `screenshot [--format png\|jpeg] [--quality N] [--scale F] [--max-size N] [--output PATH\|DIR/\|-]` | Save the screen; prints `filePath` |
| `io tap X,Y [--aim] [--count N]` | Tap; `--aim` finds the pointer and corrects before tapping |
| `io longpress X,Y [--duration MS]` | Press and hold |
| `io swipe X1,Y1,X2,Y2` | Swipe |
| `io text 'TEXT'` | Type ASCII text |
| `io keys COMBO` | Press a key or combo |
| `io button HOME` | Home Screen |
| `device info` | Board status |
| `calibrate` | Measure the pointer |
| `history list`, `history show RUN\|latest`, `history new` | What was done on the phone; start a new run |
| `intent list`, `intent show NAME`, `intent save ...`, `intent delete NAME` | Saved tasks |
| `intent export NAME [--screenshots] [--output FILE]`, `intent import FILE` | Move saved tasks to and from the iOS app |
| `upgrade [--check]`, `version` | Update the CLI; print its version |
| `mcp` | Run the MCP server on stdio |

With several boards nearby pass `--device <id>` or set `ESP32AGENT_DEVICE`.

## The see-act loop

1. Take a screenshot (`screenshot` tool, or `esp32agent screenshot` and read the PNG at `filePath`).
   It waits until the screen has settled after your last action.
2. Decide one action from what you see.
3. Do that one action, with coordinates in pixels of that full-size screenshot. If you used `--scale` or
   `--max-size`, convert the coordinates back to full size.
4. Take another screenshot and check the result before the next step. Never chain several taps blind.

Tips:
- To scroll a list, swipe up from the lower middle to the upper middle of the screen.
- To open an app: press HOME, swipe down in the middle of the Home Screen, type the app name, press `enter`.

# Manina AI: drive a real iPhone with esp32agent

An ESP32 Agent board (Manina AI) acts as the iPhone's mouse and keyboard: plugged into a USB-C iPhone (USB mode),
or as its Bluetooth mouse and keyboard on any USB power (Bluetooth mode; Lightning iPhones XS to 14 need it). The
mode is set in the iOS app (Settings > Board > Input); the CLI cannot switch it. It also receives the iPhone's AirPlay screen mirroring. Your computer reaches
the board over Bluetooth with the `esp32agent` command line tool, which is also an MCP server. No jailbreak is
needed.

iPhone only for now. iPad support is coming soon.

## Prerequisites

- A Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32S3 board (8 MB flash, 8 MB PSRAM), or a similar ESP32-S3 board with native USB.
- Board firmware v0.2.2 or later. Install it in Chrome or Edge at https://manina.ai/install
  (one USB data cable, nothing else to install). Bluetooth mode needs v0.2.7 or later with both inputs.
- On the iPhone:
  - AssistiveTouch on (Settings > Accessibility > Touch > AssistiveTouch), so the mouse pointer shows and taps.
  - Screen Mirroring to the board: join the board's Wi-Fi, then Control Center > Screen Mirroring > ESP32 Agent.
  - The phone unlocked while the agent works.
- On the computer: Bluetooth, Node.js 18 or later (for `npx`), and `ffmpeg` (needed for screenshots).

## Install

Nothing to install up front; `npx` fetches the CLI:

```sh
npx -y esp32agent version
```

Or install it globally with `npm install -g esp32agent` and call `esp32agent` directly. The examples below use
`npx -y esp32agent`; with a global install, drop the `npx -y`.

MCP server (stdio), if your agent does not already have it from this plugin:

```sh
claude mcp add esp32agent -- npx -y esp32agent mcp
```

Other MCP clients:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "esp32agent": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "esp32agent", "mcp"] } } }
```

## Pair (once per computer)

1. Power the board (USB mode: plug it into the iPhone). Within 3 minutes of it powering up run
   `npx -y esp32agent pair`. In Bluetooth mode, pair the board on the iPhone in the same window (Settings >
   Accessibility > Touch > AssistiveTouch > Devices > Bluetooth Devices); missed it, replug the board's power.
2. Start Screen Mirroring on the iPhone to ESP32 Agent.
3. `npx -y esp32agent screenshot` should now save a PNG of the phone's screen.
4. `npx -y esp32agent calibrate` measures the pointer. It also runs by itself before the earliest tap. It needs
   the pointer visible on screen.

## MCP tools

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `screenshot` | The screen now, after the last action settled. Other tools take pixel coordinates of this image |
| `tap` | Tap at `x`, `y`; `count: 2` double-taps |
| `longpress` | Press and hold at `x`, `y` (`duration_ms`, default 1000) |
| `swipe` | Swipe from `x1`, `y1` to `x2`, `y2` |
| `type_text` | Type into the focused field (ASCII; Chinese is typed as pinyin) |
| `press_key` | `enter`, `esc`, `tab`, `backspace`, `space`, arrows, `cmd+a`, `shift+tab` ... |
| `press_button` | `HOME` only (go to the Home Screen) |
| `device_info` | Board status: mirroring (`ap`), video frozen (`fz`), app busy (`busy`), `usb`, `ble`; in Bluetooth mode `hid` (`ok`/`off`) |
| `history` | `action: list` (recent runs) or `show` (one run's steps with their screenshots) |
| `intent_list`, `intent_show`, `intent_save` | Saved tasks: list, show one, save what worked |

Every tool takes an optional `device` (board id) when more than one board is nearby.

## CLI commands

Every command prints JSON: `{"status":"ok","data":...}` or `{"status":"error","error":"..."}` (exit code 1).

|---|---|
| `devices` | Boards nearby (`id`, `paired`, `connected`) |
| `pair`, `unpair` | Pair this computer with the board; forget it here |
| `screenshot [--format png\|jpeg] [--quality N] [--scale F] [--max-size N] [--output PATH\|DIR/\|-]` | Save the screen; prints `filePath` |
| `io tap X,Y [--aim] [--count N]` | Tap; `--aim` finds the pointer and corrects before tapping |
| `io longpress X,Y [--duration MS]` | Press and hold |
| `io swipe X1,Y1,X2,Y2` | Swipe |
| `io text 'TEXT'` | Type ASCII text |
| `io keys COMBO` | Press a key or combo |
| `io button HOME` | Home Screen |
| `device info` | Board status |
| `calibrate` | Measure the pointer |
| `history list`, `history show RUN\|latest`, `history new` | What was done on the phone; start a new run |
| `intent list`, `intent show NAME`, `intent save ...`, `intent delete NAME` | Saved tasks |
| `intent export NAME [--screenshots] [--output FILE]`, `intent import FILE` | Move saved tasks to and from the iOS app |
| `upgrade [--check]`, `version` | Update the CLI; print its version |
| `mcp` | Run the MCP server on stdio |

   It waits until the screen has settled after your last action.
2. Decide one action from what you see.
